messages:
alex: Heads up — invoice preview for tenant `alpha` showed -360 credits after eviction threshold applied. Think this is a routing -> metering handoff bug.

maria: Oof. Which eviction? the route-priority spillover that drops low-priority events?

alex: Yeah. We saw a burst, routing bumped to fallback pool, fallback tags get `evicted:true` in the event metadata and later the aggregator treats evicted events as refunds.

sanjay: Can you paste a raw event sample? want to confirm the field mapping we changed last month.

alex: Sure — sample from the edge:
```json
{"tenant":"alpha","route":"nlp-v2","tokens":1200,"evicted":true,"evict_reason":"priority_spill","fingerprint":"abc123","ingest_ts":1689000123}
```

emma: I think the aggregator `ingest->normalize` expects `evicted` to be `"evicted": "true"` as a string for legacy dedupe, not boolean. That mismatch could flip the logic and decrement instead of skipping.

maria: Wait how would boolean -> string flip cause a negative credit? the ledger only subtracts when `chargeable == true`.

jia: The pipeline has two places: the aggregator sets `chargeable = !evicted` (js transform) and the post-agg join with promos computes net credits. If `evicted` is truthy mismatch, the transform may coerce differently. I ran a quick REPL earlier where `!"true" == false` but `!true == false` — not helpful.

sanjay: More likely root cause: downstream mapping step `route_attrs` replaces `evicted` with `eviction_flag` and also sets `charge_delta = -tokens * multiplier` for flagged events to reflect compensation. If the flagging happens twice due to duplicate routing fingerprints, you could double-credit negative deltas.

alex: We see duplicates in the shard for that tenant; edge proxy retried, but fingerprinting should dedupe. The retry TTL was 30s and the aggregator compact window is 10s, so they both landed.

emma: Could be a fingerprint namespace collision when fallback pool rewrites route id. I filed a small test:
```sql
select fingerprint, count(*) from raw_events where tenant='alpha' and ingest_ts > 1689000000 group by fingerprint having count(*)>1;
```
Result: many duplicates where `route` differs but fingerprint same.

billing-bot: alert: invoice_preview_delta for tenant=alpha = -360 credits. Ticket #INC-4521 created.

maria: Action items: 1) stop treating `evicted` boolean as refund signal until we validate all transforms, 2) add defensive check to aggregator to ignore events with `evict_reason` present unless `eviction_ack` true, 3) backfill fix to correct any negative deltas in invoice preview.

sanjay: I'll own 1 and 2. Quick patch: make aggregator treat `evicted` only if `eviction_source == \"billing\"` and add idempotency guard using `fingerprint + ingest_ts_bucket`.

jia: For backfill, we should run a scoped reconciliation job for the affected time window and tenant. I'll sketch a query to compute suspect negative deltas and produce a reversal patch.

emma: UI/console note: we should surface a provenance tag on invoice_preview rows showing which pipeline component marked an event as refundable — that will make root cause triage easier for support.

alex: Agreed. Also add an alert when preview delta crosses 100 credits negative and link to the job.

maria: One more edge: we rolled out the routing rewrite last Friday without a compatibility flag for the metering transforms. Can we gate that behind a runtime flag so Dedicated customers don't get hit?

sanjay: Yes — I'll add a runtime flag and a canary that keeps `evicted` semantics backward-compatible for 24h.

alex: Thanks. Can someone add the small reproducer and a short note to the console runbook? I'll coordinate with billing on whether to suppress previews until backfill completes.

emma: I'll update the runbook and the invoice preview UX so it shows a temporary warning with link to INC-4521.

alex: Cool. If anyone finds other tenants with similar pattern ping me. :mag:
